title: Issued USGS aftershock forecasts for 248 earthquakes (2019-2026) gave about twice too many sequences with aftershocks in ComCat, mostly at magnitudes below the stated catalog completeness
abstract: Question: are the aftershock forecasts that the USGS Aftershock Forecasting System actually issued calibrated against the ComCat catalog? Approach: we downloaded all 14,435 archived versions of the ComCat oaf product for 252 events (2019-07 to 2026-11; median mainshock M5.0; 250 events in 2024-2026). We counted ComCat earthquakes in each forecast circle and window and scored 14,207 versions of 248 events whose windows had ended. We wrote the plan before scoring. Results: for the first issued version of each event (median 20 minutes after the mainshock), 78 sequences had an M3 or larger event in the 1-week window against 144.1 expected (ratio 0.54); the ratios were 0.51 for M4 and 0.54 for M5 (14 against 25.7, p = 0.0015). Later versions were better: with all versions and equal event weights, the 1-week ratios were 0.59 (95% cluster-bootstrap CI 0.49-0.68) for M3, 0.79 (0.64-0.90) for M4 and 0.89 (0.62-1.10) for M5. The 95% count ranges held more than 95% of counts up to 1 month, but only 86% for 1-year M3 forecasts. The issued Bayesian forecast beat the generic forecast but was worse than the sequence-specific forecast at M3. In post-hoc analyses, most of the excess was at thresholds below the catalog completeness magnitude that each run states: for M3 below it, 55 against 119.2 sequences (ratio 0.46); at or above it, 15 against 16.0 (0.94). A fitted a-value offset was -0.81 below and -0.12 (CI -0.48 to +0.14) above completeness. At complete thresholds an excess remained (M4 offset -0.39, CI -0.61 to -0.18, a factor of 2.5), mainly after M5-6 mainshocks, but forecasts after M6 or larger mainshocks and ETAS forecasts for large earthquakes were consistent with ComCat. A wider counting radius did not remove the deficit after we subtracted background. Limitations: ComCat is the truth; the stated completeness can be optimistic; the sample is mostly small 2024-2026 mainshocks, with only 16 of M6 or more and 113 with a completed 1-year window.

Grey band: 95% range if the forecasts were calibrated (Poisson-binomial simulation). Labels give observed/expected.

Observed/expected for the 1-week window, split by whether the threshold is below (orange) or at or above (blue) the catalog completeness magnitude magCat that each forecast run states. Left: first issued version; right: all versions with equal event weights. Bars: 95% cluster-bootstrap CI.

Left: a-value offset that calibrates the first issued Reasenberg-Jones forecasts (1-week window), by threshold, completeness stratum and mainshock magnitude; -0.3 is a factor of 2 in rate.
